gloss: It's not like that / Not so
Just like that / As is / Right away
Stay right there / Hold on (on phone)
Do it just like that / Do it right away
Just go and come back (casual, quick trip)
Open your eyes / Wake up (informal, often used for kids)
I'll go out and come back
I am angry (lit: to me, it is angry)
I don't like it (lit: to me, it is not pleasing)
I like it (lit: to me, it is pleasing)
I am shy / I am embarrassed (lit: to me, it is shy)
What happened? (often used to ask why someone is upset/sad)
Just kidding / Just for fun / For no reason
It's okay / Never mind / No problem
We are going to aunt's house (paternal aunt)
Is everyone well at your home? (Common greeting)
Food is ready / Rice is ready
I'll manage / I'll take care of it
You manage / You take care of it (respectful)
Might have to do / Will have to do
Might have to go / Will have to go
Let's see later. / We'll see later.
Are you coming? / Do you want to come?
What's the matter? / What's the news?
Oh no! / Alas! (expression of mild disappointment or sympathy)
Oh my god! / What a pity! (stronger expression of sympathy or shock)
Wow! / Oh my! (expression of surprise, wonder, or sometimes exasperation)
That's what I'm looking at / That's what I'm thinking (agreement/acknowledgment)
That's how it is / Exactly like that
Is that so? / Really? (general usage, but good to reinforce)
Is that so? (Kongu specific, often with a hint of surprise/skepticism)
Then? / What next? (used to prompt for more information or continue a story)
That's all / That's it (often used to conclude something or express finality)
What is it, man? / What's up? (Kongu casual, often used to get attention or inquire)
Whatever / Let it be (expression of resignation or mild annoyance)
Just / For no reason / Joking (e.g., சும்மா சொன்னேன் - I just said it / I was joking)
I will see / I will watch
What are you doing? (informal, to a friend/younger person)
I am asking / I am listening
I am reading / I am studying
I am seeing / I am looking
Very / a lot — the universal intensifier (locked in 5 deck chunks)
Side / direction — வலது பக்கம், இடது பக்கம்
This (before a noun) — இந்த சட்டை எவ்ளோ?
Do / make (bare root; common spoken alternative to செய்)
Give (bare imperative / root; spoken form of கொடு)
Start / set off / leave (Oracle: always 'kelambu' in Coimbatore speech, never literary 'purappadu')
Open (Oracle: canonical root is 'thira', colloquially pronounced 'thora')
Wash / rinse with water (bare imperative / root)
Wipe / clean a surface (Oracle: root is 'thudai', not 'thodai' which means thigh)
Put in / drop / wear (bare imperative / root)
Take off clothing or shoes (Oracle: spoken 'kazhatu', never literary 'kazhatru')
Be available / obtain (Oracle: canonical root is 'kidai', not 'keda' which means spoil)
Pay attention / notice / care for (bare root)
Climb / board a bus or vehicle (bare root)
Descend / get off a vehicle (bare root)
Wait patiently / bear with (bare imperative / root)
Heat up / be burning hot (bare root)
Protect / rescue / look after (Oracle: spoken 'kaappaathu', never literary 'kaappatru')
Fill a container (Oracle: canonical root is 'nirappu', colloquially 'nerappu')
Reduce / lower / decrease (compound sense: transitive and intransitive)
Must / need to (bound obligation suffix on verb stem; Oracle: spoken '-num', never literary '-vendum' or '-vendiyadhu')
Must not / should not (bound prohibitive auxiliary)
Cannot / unable to (bound negative potential; Oracle: always 'mudiyala' in speech, never 'mudiyavillai')
May / let's (bound suggestion and permissive auxiliary)
Keep on doing (bound continuous/habitual aspect; Oracle: spoken '-tte iru', never literary '-kondiru')
Do definitively / completive aspect auxiliary (attached to adverbial participle)
Try doing / test out (tentative auxiliary attached to participle, e.g. saaptu paaru)
Do in advance / preparatory aspect auxiliary (attached to participle, e.g. solli vai)
Elapsed / completed state auxiliary (Oracle: e.g. time aachu, saaptaachu)
Has not become / not yet auxiliary (Oracle: spoken 'aagala', never 'aagavillai')
Don't want / no need modal predicate (Oracle: spoken 'vendaam' or 'venaam')
Don't know / not visible (experiencer modal; Oracle: spoken 'theriyala', not 'theriyavillai')
Don't understand (experiencer modal; Oracle: spoken 'puriyala', not 'puriyavillai')
Will not (negative future auxiliary, 1st person singular)
Will not (negative future auxiliary, 3rd person plural / honorific)
Accidental or abrupt completion auxiliary (attached to participle, e.g. thoongitaaru)
Benefactive auxiliary - do for someone else (attached to participle, e.g. senju kudu)
Exasperated completion auxiliary (used when annoyed, e.g. solli tholay)
Doesn't feel like / doesn't occur to mind (experiencer modal; e.g. enakku thonala)
To / for (bound dative case clitic; attached to noun/pronoun stems)
In / at / on (bound locative case clitic; Oracle: spoken '-la', never literary '-il')
Of / with (bound genitive/associative clitic; Oracle: spoken '-oda', replaces literary '-udaiya')
Along with (bound sociative clitic; e.g. avanga kooda)
Direct object marker (bound accusative clitic; Oracle: spoken '-a', replaces literary '-ai')
By / because of (bound instrumental and causal clitic; Oracle: spoken '-aala', replaces '-aal')
From (bound ablative case clitic; Oracle: in speech pronounced '-lerundhu')
Near / with an animate entity (bound locative clitic; Oracle: replaces literary '-idathil')
Respectful honorific clitic (Oracle: signature Coimbatore polite address, e.g. vaanga-nga)
Isn't it? / right? (tag confirmation clitic; Oracle: spoken '-dhaane', never literary 'allava')
Only / indeed (emphatic focus clitic; Oracle: spoken '-dhaan')
Affectionate conversational address clitic (informal paternal / friendly filler)
Affectionate address clitic (female / child / gentle request, e.g. saapdu-ma)
Yes/no question interrogative clitic (attached to sentence predicate, e.g. varumaa?)
Intimate casual address clitic (Oracle: male peer or child only; never use with elders)
Emphatic vowel lengthening clitic (e.g. avare sonnaaru)
Above / on top / upstairs (Oracle: spoken 'mela', replaces literary 'mele')
Below / down / on the floor (Oracle: spoken 'keezha', replaces literary 'keezhe')
In front of / ahead (Oracle: spoken 'munnaadi', replaces literary 'munbe')
Behind / in back (Oracle: spoken 'pinnaadi', replaces literary 'pinbe')
Nearby / next to (Oracle: spoken 'pakkathula', replaces literary 'arugil')
At the edge / corner of the room or road
Therefore / that's why (Oracle: spoken 'adhanaale', never literary 'aagaiyaal')
Already / in that short time (expresses pacing or surprise)
Otherwise / or else (Oracle: spoken 'illaatti', replaces literary 'illaiyel')
Afterwards / and then / what next? (Oracle: spoken 'apram', never literary 'pinbu')
At that time / then in that case
Definitely / for sure (Oracle: spoken 'kandippa', replaces literary 'nichayamaaga')
The thing is / what happened is (conversational topic introducer)
For that purpose / on that account
For what reason / why (Oracle: spoken 'edhukku', more practical than 'yen')
Until where / up to which point
Well / thoroughly / good (Oracle: spoken 'nalla', never literary 'nandraaga')
Never mind / that's okay / don't mention it (Oracle: spoken 'paravaala')
Congratulations / best wishes (Oracle: standard modern spelling)
We (inclusive of listener; Oracle: distinction between inclusive 'namma' and exclusive 'naanga' is vital)
They / she respectful (Oracle: spoken 'avanga', replaces literary 'avargal')
He respectful / elder (Oracle: spoken 'avaru', respectful reference for elders/in-laws)
